_comment: FITTED CONSTANTS FOR THIS PHYSICAL ROBOT — calibration data, not defaults.
They lived on the systemd unit's ExecStart, which the BOM doc (§9.2, §3.3) flags as
the wrong home twice over: a value invisible to anyone reading the docs, and one that
the checked-in unit did not carry, so reinstalling it silently dropped the ToF
calibration. Both now live here, the way servo_map.json and poses.json already do,
so they travel with the robot and BOTH programs read the same number.
CLI flags still override, for bench work.

tof._why: The VL53L0X is recessed up inside the chassis so the belly's 0-56 mm working range sits above the part's unreliable short end. Anchored at BELLY-DOWN, which folds the part's own 8-11 mm long-reading bias into the offset and puts the calibration at the dangerous end of the channel. Re-fit after any belly re-assembly.

ina219._why: At 10 mOhm the trace and solder resistance are a material fraction of the shunt, so this is a fitted value rather than the part's nominal. Raw counts are what get recorded; this only derives amps, so a re-fit can re-derive already-captured samples.

ground_clearance._why: The normalizer the promoted height homeostat rides: published signal = clamp(raw_m / stand_m, 0, 1). MUST match the sim's GROUND_CLEARANCE_STAND or the robot feeds a differently-scaled number into a promoted lever. Shared implementation: ogma::body::ground_clearance().

imu._why: Chip-frame body-up with the belly flat on a level floor (BOM §4.2: five placements over four verified 180° rotations, 0.05° repeatability, floor slope 0.49° subtracted out). It lumps mount tilt together with accelerometer bias, unsplit, and is applied to the ACCELEROMETER ONLY. Icm20948Config's default carries the same 2026-09-10 fit and its comment asked for exactly this file; re-fit after any IMU remount.
